Frames VICE_SHM_PATH->shm (the same IFB1 wire format drawshm uses), keys vicectl + the shared us-layout keysym table, audio -sounddev wav -> FIFO. Launcher stations/vice-native/x11-runtime.sh; reset=relaunch restores the checkpoint in /data/vms/streamhost/stations/pet2001/sta/golden.vsf.

render.stationsManifestPrelude: # pet2001 — host-native VICE 3.10.0 xpet -model 2001 (Commodore PET 2001, 1977) -> COMMODORE BASIC. De-bridged 2026-08-16: no QEMU, no guest, no X, no ssh. Keyboard-only. Same binary as cbm8032, different model.

museum.blurb: One of the three machines that started the personal-computer industry in 1977, and the only one that arrived as a single sealed box: screen, keyboard and cassette deck welded into one sheet-metal trapezoid you could carry home and switch on.
museum.notes: Live streamhost tile, and the oldest machine in the gallery. Emulator-in-captured-Linux BRIDGE tile: a captured Debian 13 (trixie) kiosk runs VICE (xpet -model 2001) emulating the ORIGINAL 1977 PET; streamhost captures the Linux framebuffer + AC97 audio exactly like every other tile. VICE bundles the Commodore ROMs, so this tile needs no external media. VICE's model 2001 is the real machine and not a badge — RamSize=8, Crtc=0 (it predates the 6545 CRTC every later PET used), VideoSize=40, the chiclet graphics keyboard, the 2001-blueish phosphor palette. The golden is the machine's own untouched power-on screen; the exhibit's interaction is the SPA type-in demo, four lines of PET BASIC that POKE characters straight into screen memory at 32768, which is how the PET drew everything. Keyboard-only exhibit (unshifted keys give upper case, SHIFT gives the graphics set, hence keyboard.letterCase=upper-only). See streamhost/docs/BRIDGE.md and docs/guests/pet2001.md.

reset.fixture: Commodore PET 2001 (1977) cold power-on screen (“*** COMMODORE BASIC *** / 7167 BYTES FREE / READY.”), HOST-NATIVE: VICE 3.10.0's xpet -model 2001 runs on the host, headless, and publishes the emulated screen straight into the shm mapping at 768x432 (-CRTCdsize; there is no -CRTCborders, VICE's CRTC video code has none). resetMode=relaunch, and this station COLD-BOOTS: the launcher restarts xpet with VICE_NATIVE_CHECKPOINT=0 and no checkpoint is restored, because restoring a CRTC machine's snapshot CHANGES THE PUBLISHED SURFACE — 768x432 becomes 768x552, the restored CRTC register state resolving to a different screen size than the one the ROM programs. A live station whose geometry moves on reset is not shippable. Measured 2026-08-16; a cold boot is stable to 120 M cycles. The exhibit loses nothing, because the scene IS an untouched cold boot. Keys resolve through PET/gtk3_grus_sym.vkm, the GRAPHICS keyboard — this station and cbm8032 share the xpet binary and share no keyboard at all. Keyboard-only exhibit (no mouse); PET sound -> FIFO.
